subject: Clarifying commit bands, streaming rounding, and short-term proration
messages:
From: Aiden Park <aiden@helix.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@helix.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on how Redwood counts streaming tokens and commit proration

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Helix is excited about the latency profile. Before procurement signs off we need a crisp definition of how billable tokens are computed for streaming responses, and how commit bands / proration work if we ramp mid-quarter. A few specific asks:

- For streaming (server-sent tokens over many frames), do you round per frame, per chunk, or only at the final aggregated token count? Helix uses long-lived streams (avg 18s) and is sensitive to rounding rules.
- If we commit to a quarterly volume band, and in month 1 we consume only 40% of that month’s portion, will unused volume carry forward, or is there a true-up at quarter end?
- Is there a grace window or “buffer credits” you can offer during the first 30 days while we optimize prompts?

Procurement also asked for a simple example calculation we can include with the SOW. Could you share a short explainer and a one-paragraph contract clause we can drop into the SOW?

Appreciate it — copying procurement.

— Aiden

---

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Aiden Park <aiden@helix.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on how Redwood counts streaming tokens and commit proration

Aiden — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kar (pricing) and Marcus (contracts) to confirm the formal language. Below is a concise explainer + suggested SOW clause and a sample calculation.

Short explainer (plain English):
- Billable tokens are computed at the request level: every request contribution (prompt + generated tokens) is counted. For streaming responses we maintain a single per-request token tally and only round at the request granularity at the time of billing. We do not round per-frame. That means partial frames are accumulated into the request total; the per-request token count is what maps to the commit band. This reduces rounding inflation for long-lived streams.

- Commit bands / proration: Quarterly commits are allocated evenly by day across the quarter. If you under-use a month, unused volume remains in your quarterly pool and can be consumed later in the quarter. At quarter-end we apply a true-up: if total quarter usage is below the committed quantity we do not issue a credit (commits are prepaid/committed discounts), but we will discuss carry-forward for large enterprise deals on a case-by-case basis.

- Grace / buffer credits: For first-time commitments we offer a one-time on-ramp buffer equal to 5% of the commit for the first 30 days to help with prompt tuning. This is granted as non-refundable consumption credits that count toward the commit.

Suggested SOW clause (draft):
"Metering and Billing: Billable units are calculated per-request by aggregating prompt and generation tokens for each API invocation. For streaming responses, token usage is aggregated at the request level (no per-frame rounding). Quarterly committed volume is allocated pro rata across the quarter by day. Unused daily allocations remain in the quarter pool and may be consumed later in the same quarter. Committed discounts apply to the total quarterly usage at invoice time. First-time quarterly commits are eligible for a one-time on-ramp buffer credit equal to 5% of the committed quantity for the initial 30-day tuning window. Credits are applied to consumption and are non-refundable."

Example calculation (simple):
- Commitment: 9,000,000 tokens / quarter (3,000,000 tokens / month equivalent) with 20% discount band applied.
- Day allocation for a 90-day quarter: 9,000,000 / 90 = 100,000 tokens/day
- Week 1 actual usage: 550,000 tokens (averaged 78,571 tokens/day)
- Month 1 total usage: 800,000 tokens (under monthly pro rata 3,000,000), remaining quarter pool = 9,000,000 - 800,000 = 8,200,000 tokens
- Billing: At quarter close we apply the 20% discount to the total quarter usage (e.g., if final quarter usage = 8,600,000 tokens, invoice is computed on 8,600,000 with applied Tier pricing).

Attached is a short PDF that visualizes rolling pool behavior and the Draft-Commit-Terms doc with contract text we typically use. Kar/Marcus — please flag any legal or finance concerns.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, GTM Pricing
Redwood Inference

---

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, Aiden Park <aiden@helix.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on how Redwood counts streaming tokens and commit proration

Aiden — quick follow-up from pricing ops: two additional clarifications that procurement typically asks for.

1) Rounding behavior for crediting versus billing: When we apply buffer credits or promotional credits we deduct those at the invoice level after aggregating total usage. We do not retroactively re-slice per-request rounding; the internal token math remains integer-based at final aggregation.

2) Short quarter ramp: If Helix signs mid-quarter we prorate the committed quantity by days remaining (rounded up to the nearest 1,000 tokens for the commit allocation). Example: 45 days left in quarter with 4,500,000 quarter commit => you are allocated 2,250,000 tokens (rounded up to 2,251,000 for commit accounting). This rounding is only for determining commit band eligibility, not per-request billing.

We also offer an optional smoothing clause where we set a floor usage for month 1 (e.g., 50% of month slice) in exchange for a slightly shallower discount ramp — happy to model both.

— Kar

---

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Aiden Park <aiden@helix.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on how Redwood counts streaming tokens and commit proration

Aiden,

Thanks for raising the procurement questions. To make this easy to drop into your SOW we've added two short bullets Marcus-style (legal-friendly) below; these are safe to include but we can tighten language in the final MSA if you prefer.

Contract-friendly bullets (ready to paste into SOW):
- "Usage Measurement. Billable usage equals aggregated token counts (prompt + generation) per API invocation. For streaming responses, tokens are aggregated per request and reported as a single integer; no per-frame rounding shall increase the reported count for that request."
- "Commit Allocation and Proration. Committed quantities for a quarter are allocated pro rata by day across the quarter. If the operative SOW commences mid-quarter, the committed quantity will be prorated by the number of days remaining in the quarter. Proration for commit band computation will be rounded up to the nearest 1,000 tokens."

We will also accept the 5% initial buffer credit for the first 30 days as a one-time concession for this deal — we'll include it as a line item in the SOW appendix (non-refundable, counts toward committed usage).

If procurement confirms these bullets are acceptable I'll get the SOW patch over to DocuSign this afternoon.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Aiden Park <aiden@helix.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@helix.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on how Redwood counts streaming tokens and commit proration

Tessa / Kar / Marcus — this is perfect and very clear. Procurement confirms the proration and the 1,000-token rounding rule look fine; they asked two small follow-ups: 

1) Can the 5% buffer be consumed within the first 45 days instead of 30? We expect slower prompt tuning across a team ramp.
2) Will the DocuSign SOW include a worked example like the numbers you provided? Procurement wants that embedded.

If you can accept 45 days we can get signatures this afternoon.

— Aiden
